rules.title: Loop control signal
rules.body: Branch only on stop_reason (tool_use vs end_turn). Never parse assistant text for intent, and never use an iteration counter as the primary termination mechanism — it's a safety cap, not the control flow.

rules.title: Choosing an orchestration pattern
rules.body: Ordered, predictable subtasks → prompt chaining. Distinct input categories → routing. Independent subtasks or need for consensus → parallelization. Unpredictable decomposition → orchestrator-workers. Clear quality bar, generation alone unreliable → evaluator-optimizer.

rules.title: Subagent communication
rules.body: Hub-and-spoke only. Subagents talk to the orchestrator, never to each other. A subagent returns a final result, not its full transcript.

rules.title: Context to give a subagent
rules.body: The minimum needed for its scoped task — not the orchestrator's full history. Isolation protects focus and token cost.

rules.title: Default failure mode to avoid
rules.body: Treating premature termination (stopping before tool_use resolves) and infinite fallback loops (never respecting a real end_turn) as equally likely exam traps — both come from not trusting stop_reason alone.

rules.title: What makes a good tool
rules.body: A precise, example-rich description matters more than a clever name. The model chooses tools based on the description text.

rules.title: tool_use vs tool_result
rules.body: tool_use is emitted by the model (request to call). tool_result is sent by the client (the outcome), matched by id.

rules.title: MCP vocabulary
rules.body: Server = exposes capabilities. Client = 1:1 connection to a server. Host = the application (e.g. Claude Code) managing multiple clients. Primitives = Tools (model-invoked), Resources (contextual data), Prompts (templates).

rules.title: Transport choice
rules.body: Local/trusted process → stdio. Remote or shared → Streamable HTTP.

rules.title: Error handling
rules.body: Always return structured, actionable errors (is_error:true + clear message) — never a raw stack trace — so the model can self-correct on retry.

rules.title: Built-in tool vs MCP vs skill
rules.body: One-off local capability → built-in tool if one exists. Shared/external system integration → MCP server. Team workflow, no external system → skill or slash command.

rules.title: CLAUDE.md hierarchy
rules.body: Enterprise → user → project → local. All applicable levels are merged into context — a more specific file adds to the others, it does not replace them.

rules.title: Slash command vs skill
rules.body: Slash command: user types it explicitly. Skill: Claude decides on its own to invoke it based on relevance. If the scenario needs autonomous judgment, it's a skill.

rules.title: Hooks vs prompted instructions
rules.body: Use a hook when behavior must be deterministic and non-negotiable (e.g. always run linter before commit). A prompted instruction alone is not reliable enough for hard requirements.

rules.title: Plan mode
rules.body: Use when changes are risky, hard to reverse, or need human sign-off before execution. It is read-only until explicitly approved.

rules.title: Permissions design
rules.body: Grant the narrowest permission set that still lets the workflow complete — not blanket allow, not blanket ask.

rules.title: Headless / CI use
rules.body: Non-interactive runs need permissions configured up front; there's no interactive prompt to fall back on mid-run.

rules.title: Where instructions live
rules.body: System prompt: role, constraints, behavior for the whole conversation. User message: per-turn task/content. Don't put per-turn specifics in the system prompt.

rules.title: When to use few-shot
rules.body: Desired output format is precise but hard to describe in words — show, don't just tell.

rules.title: When to use chain-of-thought
rules.body: Genuinely multi-step reasoning tasks. Skip it for simple lookups or classification — it adds latency/cost without benefit.

rules.title: Guaranteeing format
rules.body: Prefill the start of the response (e.g. with {) to force structure at the source, then validate the full output against a schema.

rules.title: Handling invalid structured output
rules.body: Re-prompt with the specific validation error, not a generic 'try again.' A bare retry tends to repeat the same mistake.

rules.title: Batch vs real-time
rules.body: Large non-interactive workload, latency not critical → Batches API. Anything a user is waiting on → standard synchronous call.

rules.title: Self-review anti-pattern
rules.body: A single call asked to generate and then check its own work tends to rubber-stamp itself. Use a separate call/pass for review.

rules.title: What counts against the context budget
rules.body: System prompt + tool definitions + retrieved data + conversation history — all of it, not just the visible chat text.

rules.title: Prompt caching mechanics
rules.body: Only the stable prefix before the first change is reused. Append new content after the cached prefix to keep hitting cache.

rules.title: Compaction trade-off
rules.body: Summarize to free space, but don't over-compact — the 'summarization trap' drops details the model still needs, producing vague later answers.

rules.title: Escalate vs proceed
rules.body: Escalate to a human when the decision is high-stakes AND hard to reverse AND confidence is low. Routine, reversible calls don't need escalation.

rules.title: Error propagation choice
rules.body: Match the response to criticality: halt on errors that invalidate the task, retry on transient ones, degrade-and-continue on non-critical ones. Never a single blanket policy.

rules.title: Idempotency
rules.body: Required for any tool call that might be automatically retried — guard non-idempotent actions (sending a message, charging a card) explicitly.

rules.title: Codebase exploration strategy
rules.body: Targeted grep/search before reading whole files. Reflexively reading an entire large repo wastes context budget the exam expects you to protect.
